key_insight: HAMLET reframes optimization as dissipative Hamiltonian motion, where loss is potential energy, geometry comes from a metric, and training follows energy-dissipating dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This geometric view can improve optimizer design by exposing how curvature, dissipation, and parameterization affect convergence and stability in practical ML training.
method: Formulate optimization as a variational Hamiltonian system with a positive-definite metric on parameter space.
Add metric-compatible Rayleigh dissipation to obtain monotonic energy decay during training.
Compare dynamics on a controlled CIFAR-10 reconstruction problem using an image Hessian metric and an MPS reparameterization to reveal geometric forces and contraction behavior.
evidence_signal: In a five-seed MNIST MLP benchmark, HAMLET achieved the highest mean test accuracy (97.95%) and the lowest mean test negative log-likelihood (0.0696) among the three evaluated optimizers.
watch_item: The framework depends on choosing or estimating a suitable metric, and position-dependent metrics may add computational and implementation complexity.
paper_title: Hamiltonian Metric Learning and Energy-Based Training: A Dissipative Geometric Framework for Optimization
